explanation: The pole fires at word-internal token boundaries: its largest activations (1.5-1.9) sit on the second and later pieces of a multi-token word (Eur|asia, St|reptococcus, rhod|odend|ron, euc|aly|ptus, bureauc|rac|ies), on a digit group inside a longer number (in 17|25), and on the period of a single-letter abbreviation (the U|.|S., Mr|.) once the text already contains an earlier sentence boundary ('.' or newline); word onsets of ordinary content words stay near the corpus baseline of 0.04. A weaker companion family (0.2-0.8) covers a learned set of clause-level operators - negation/approximation/contrast/limitation words such as while, whereas, nearly, almost, never, until, too, still, and the prepositions at/from/near - but not the/a/of/in/and/is/to/with/for (all <= 0.035); this family is not a word-internal split, so the split rule explains the peak strengths while the operators remain a related offshoot.
